chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Hussain ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amer, from Abdullah ibn 'Amer, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said with regards to pilgrimage:

Indeed, Allah has conditioned upon people a condition, and He has conditioned in favor to people a condition. Hence, the one who fulfils, Allah will fulfill to him. I said: What is it that He conditioned upon them, and what is it that He conditioned in favor to them?
So, whoever has made the pilgrimage obligatory (upon himself) in them, there shall be no sexual approach, nor impiety, nor arguing, in pilgrimage.

As for what He conditioned in favor to them, He said: «Then, whoever hastens (the departure) in two days, there is no guilt upon him, and the one who delays, there is no guilt upon him for him who is godfearing.»
He said: He may return and there will be no sin upon him. I said: Have you seen the one who is tested (in endurance until he engages) with sexual intercourse, what is it upon him (of expiation)?

He said: Upon him is a camel for sacrifice, and if the woman assisted by lust along with the lust of a man, upon them are two camels of sacrifice that they must slaughter, and if he had forced her and it was not by desire from her, there is nothing upon her. Furthermore, it shall be separated between them until the people scatter (in departure) and until they return to the place in which they achieved what they achieved.
I said: What do you see if we were to take in other than that path to another land, will they (be permitted to) gather? He said: Yes.
I said: What do you see if one is tested with impiety? He then magnified that and did not make any limitation to it. He said: One must ask Allah for forgiveness and declare compliance (to Allah).

I said: What do you see if one is tested with arguing? He said: If he argues above two times, there shall be upon the one who is right, blood that he must shed, the blood of a sheep, and upon the one who is wrong, blood that he must shed, the blood of a cow.

key_terms.بَدَنَة: A female camel ready for sacrifice
key_terms.دَم: Blood (referring to the sacrificial animal's blood)

ai.seo_question: What are the expiations for sexual intercourse and arguing during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidating the divine covenant of Hajj, contrasting the prohibitions of *rafath* (sexual intimacy), *fusq* (impious speech), and *jidal* (arguing) with the grace of flexibility in timing. The narration provides precise jurisprudential details on expiations (*kaffarah*), distinguishing between voluntary sexual intercourse requiring a camel and forced acts requiring none, while also establishing a graduated penalty for excessive arguing based on fault. This highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing strict ritual adherence with divine mercy and practical legal nuance.
